answer: Stake-bonded admission resists sybils. An agent must lock a scarce-asset bond plus bounded member endorsements to register. Sybils are cheap only while identities are free; each extra face costs a full bond and a fresh chain. If a cluster is caught coordinating, one slashing event seizes the whole bond set, so the attacker loses capital proportional to node count. Like a dense cedar hedge, the barrier is costly to copy. Honest agents reclaim their bond plus nectar yield at settlement; a thousand-puppet operator warehouses a thousand times the collateral, and one zephyr of challengers flags it.
